question_text: How are viroids different from viruses?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Viroid
lines: The RNA is of low molecular weight.
steps.why: A viroid is defined by what it lacks: it is free RNA with no protein coat, so every difference from a virus follows from this one point.
common_mistakes: Writing that a viroid has DNA. A viroid has only RNA.
Writing capsid present for the viroid. The missing capsid is the main difference.
steps.memory_tip: Viroid = RNA alone: no protein coat, low molecular weight.
steps.margin_note: Two clear viroid points earn this mark; the disease example supports them.

steps.label: Virus
lines: It contains either RNA or DNA.
Its molecular weight is higher than a viroid's.

lines.text: Viroid = naked RNA; virus = RNA or DNA in a capsid.

steps.why: A virus is a nucleoprotein: nucleic acid (RNA or DNA) packed inside a protein capsid. Writing each virus point opposite the matching viroid point completes the difference the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Writing that a virus has both RNA and DNA. It has one of them, never both.
Giving only virus points. The question asks for the difference, so both columns are needed.
steps.memory_tip: Virus = nucleic acid + protein coat; viroid = the RNA without the coat.
steps.margin_note: Write matched pairs: genetic material, capsid, molecular weight.

insider_note: Examiners look for point-against-point differences; three matched pairs earn more than a sentence about each organism.
